verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026... off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the west coast'; R5: 'splashing down in the Pacific Ocean... off the coast of southern California'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm successful splashdown in Pacific off San Diego on or around April 10, 2026 (R3 explicit date, others consistent with timeline from April 1 launch).

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the return of the first crewed lunar voyage in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972'; R2: 'marking humanity’s return to the vicinity of the Moon for the first time in more than 50 years'; R5: 'NASA's first Moon mission since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Artemis II as first crewed mission to Moon/vicinity since 1972, over 50 years.

verifications.claim: Re-entry video shows the Artemis II capsule descending under parachutes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Video of the capsule descending under parachutes also popped on the big screens'; R4: 'Watch the Artemis II re-entry: Separation, blackout, then splashdown'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly describes video of capsule under parachutes; R4 is a video source covering re-entry to splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown was a "perfect bullseye" landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'splashing down in the Pacific Ocean in a "perfect bullseye"'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing matches R5 description of the splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R2: 'Splashdown... 8:07 p.m. EDT... 8:07 p.m.: ... splash down'; R3: 'around 8:07 p.m. ET... April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm exact time 8:07 p.m. EDT/ET and date April 10, 2026, precisely for Artemis II splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown occurred in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'Pacific Ocean... off the coast of San Diego, California'; R5: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of southern California'
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly specify Pacific Ocean off/near San Diego, California.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972... first humans toward the Moon since 1972'; R2: 'sending the first humans toward the Moon since 1972'; R5: 'NASA's first Moon mission since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly identify Artemis II as first crewed Moon mission/flight since 1972.
